text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Consumer confidence reaches highest level this year in September. (page 1)

- Parliament wants to question Liberal (VVD) parliamentary party leader Frits Bolkestein about alleged conflict of interests arising from his role as member of supervisory board of Dutch unit of U.S. drugs giant Merck Sharp & Dohme. (p1)
- ABN AMRO bank takes over British venture capital company Causeway Group. (p1)
- European Commission probes planned merger of Nedlloyd and P&O's container shipping activities. (p3)
- Privatisation of information technology company Roccade likely to be delayed until 1997. (p3)
- Builder NBM-Amstelland negotiates sale of its Filamat unit to a subsidiary of France's Saint-Gobain. (p3)
- Retailer Ahold sells 12 supermarkets and two sites in northeast U.S. to Britain's Sainsbury. (p3)
- Dutch central bank (DNB) plans to extend its supervisory role to include "nature funds" investing in teak forests, diamonds etc. (p13)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Netherlands opposes a second term for U.N. secretary- gerneral Boutros Boutros Ghali. (p1)
- Korea's Samsung starts last round of talks with Fokker receivers on taking over the bankrupt planemaker. (p2)
- Delays hit planned merger of bathroom ceramics producer Sphinx Gustavsberg with Swiss Keramik Laufen. (p17) DE TELEGRAAF
- Dutch unit of U.S. drugs giant Merck Sharp & Dohme "very satisfied" with Liberal (VVD) leader Frits Bolkestein's efforts on behalf of the company. (p1)
- Pharmaceutical industry organisation Nefarma blames health minister for unavailability of new drugs that are widely available elsewhere in Europe. (p3)
- Dutch unit of Italy's troubled Olivetti electronics group does not rule out a change of name. (p27)
- Robeco Effectenbank to be wound up at end of this year. (p28)
TROUW
- Health insurer Zilveren Kruis to launch mail order pharmacy service this year. (p1)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- European Commission investigates Schiphol airport's policy of charging passengers an anti-pollution levy. (p1)
- Netherlands' biggest flower exporter Zurel & Co in joint- venture with Chinese partner. (p11)
